data.one_liner: Folder-based route manager inspired by NextJS for Flutter applications.
data.what_it_does: Automatically creates and manages routes in your Flutter app by organizing files and folders within specific directories. It provides navigation methods, nested navigation through layouts, dynamic routes, route groups, and middleware support.
use_when: You prefer a folder-based file structure for defining routes inspired by NextJS.
You want automated route generation based on your project directory layout.
You need nested navigation, custom transitions, and route guards/middlewares.
avoid_when: You prefer a purely declarative or code-first routing approach without file-system mapping.
Your project relies on an existing router configuration from the given alternatives like go_router or auto_route.
strengths: Object notation support via `routePaths` for type-safe route access.
Built-in support for route groups, layouts with `RouterOutlet`, and middleware.
weaknesses: Requires running a generator command (`dart run routefly`) when adding new pages.
Strictly tied to a specific folder layout structure.
data.setup_notes: Add the package, annotate the main widget with `@Main('lib/app')`, configure `MaterialApp.router` with `Routefly.routerConfig`, and run `dart run routefly` to generate routes.

alternatives.name: go_router
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides a declarative routing package officially backed and widely adopted in the Flutter ecosystem.

alternatives.name: auto_route
alternatives.why_pick_it: Offers powerful code-generated routing with strong typing for parameters and deep linking.

alternatives.name: beamer
alternatives.why_pick_it: Focuses on URI-based navigation and delegate-based routing for complex multi-screen apps.
